chapter: Leaving Hampton and starting his own band
title: The Zanzibar in Philadelphia and Gale Agency's Ralph Cooper
summary: His two-week Philadelphia job packs the club, agents Ralph Cooper and Lou Leslie hear him, and Cooper pushes him over breakfast to sign with Gale Agency instead of resting.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And I got away from it. And the results of this, now, let me get into it. I played in the [White] Zanzibar in Philadelphia. Gale Agency called over. Lou Leslie was the guy -- about putting in a group in the [WHITE] Zanzibar. So Dick told them, said, "Man, we got the best attraction we could have in here. We don't need nobody now." He I said, "Who do you have?" He said, "We got Arnett Cobb from Lionel Hampton's band. He's packing them in." Say, "He is?" I'm just going to work for two weeks, and I'm going to rest six months. I'm really going to rest six months on my back.

Do you know that night they was there? Ralph Cooper, Lou Leslie and Tim Gales come in to hear what he was talking about on the telephone. And when he come in and heard the group, they asked him could -- on intermission -- could we take the group over to one of them halls on Broad Street because he had a band sound in there, and they permitted it. And we went over there.
They had drums and all that set up, where you didn't have to take no instrument other than your horn, you know.

And so Ralph Cooper, they put Ralph Cooper on there. And I -- they asked me when would I be in New York. I said, 'Well, Sunday, you know, we blacked out here, and I'm coming on in and come back Monday for the second week.' He said, 'I'd like to have breakfast with you at Frank's, 125th Street.' So okay. So I had breakfast with him at 10:00 that Monday morning. He was talking to me about signing a contract, coming in often and whatever. I said, 'Well, Ralph, I don't know.' I said, 'that's not really my plan. My plan is to rest.' He said, 'Well, baby -- that was his word, baby -- we -- I can do a lot for you up there,' you know, and blah-blah-blah. I said, 'Okay, we'll talk about it.' I go on playing my next week and close down, and we meet again on the next Monday after Philadelphia, which I'm off Sunday resting, and all that. I'm all right.
And we talked. He wanted to go up to the office and (inaudible).
Ralph Cooper, he was a location booker.
